Background | Information

Background Information | In | film | and | television | works, | we | often | hear | Traditional | Chinese | timekeeping | methods | such | as | a | stick | of | incense, | a | cup | of | tea, | etc | . | Do | you | know | how | long | they | each | represent? | In | ancient | China, | a | day | was | divided | into | twelve | units, | each | equal | to | two | hours | today | . | And | further | divisions | were | made | on | this | basis | to | make | the | time | more | precise | .

Background Information | There | are | twelve | hours | in | a | day, | and | one | hour | is | two | hours | of | modern | time | ; | one | hour | has | eight | quarters, | and | one | quarter | is | 15 | minutes | of | modern | time | ; | one | quarter | has | three | tea | time, | one | tea | time | is | five | minutes | of | modern | time | ; | one | tea | time | has | two | sticks | of | incense, | the | time | of | one | stick | of | incense | is | 2 | minutes | and | 30 | seconds | ; | the | time | of | one | stick | of | incense | is | 5 | minutes, | and | the | time | of | one | minute | is | 30 | seconds | ; | Second | . | These | are | all | modern | people's | calculations | of | ancient | timekeeping | . | In | fact, | the | error | began | to | increase | after | the | "one | quarter" | of | the | ancient | time | unit | .

Background Information | In | order | to | improve | timing | accuracy, | ancient | scientists | invented | many | different | types | of | timing | tools, | among | which | the | Water | Clock | is | a | typical | representative, | and | the | timing | is | carried | out | in | the | form | of | flowing | water | . | Part | of | the | data | records | that | the | accuracy | of | the | Water | Clock | is | 20 | seconds | per | day, | which | was | quite | a | remarkable | timekeeping | tool | at | that | time | .
Knowledge  | Introduction

Knowledge Introduction | The | word | ³FRXQWGRZQ´ | comes | from | the | 1927 | German | fantasy | feature | film | 㸪 | The | Moon | Maid | . | In | this | film, | director | Frieze | designed | the | launch | program | of | " | 9 | , | 8 | , | 7 | , | ... | 3 | , | 2 | , | 1 | " | ignition | in | the | shot | of | the | rocket | launch | in | order | to | increase | the | artistic | effect | and | be | exciting | .

Knowledge Introduction | This | program | has | been | unanimously | praised | by | rocket | experts, | who | believe | that | it | is | very | accurate, | clear | and | scientifically | highlights | the | dwindling | time | of | the | rocket | launch, | and | makes | people | feel | a | sense | of | urgency | before | the | rocket | launch | . | Since | then, | "countdown" | has | been | widely | adopted, | and | has | surpassed | the | scope | of | use, | becoming | a | term | with | strong | applicability | and | a | wide | range | of | applications | .

Knowledge Introduction | Not | only | for | rocket | launches, | we | also | need | to | use | countdowns | reasonably | in | our | daily | lives | to | precisely | control | things | such | as | cooking, | crossing | the | road, | and | trains | entering | stations | . | Today, | we | will | use | the | dot | matrix | screen | to | make | a | precise | countdown | machine | .

Practice | Programming | logo | 02 | Function | - | Display | Define | the | "display" | function, | the | single | - | digit | is | the | remainder | after | dividing | by | 10 | , | and | the | tens | digit | is | the | rounding | down | after | dividing | by | 10 | . | Suppose | the | current | countdown | is | 30 | , | the | single | - | digit | displays | 0 | , | and | the | tens | digit | displays | 3 | ; | when | the | countdown | becomes | 29 | , | the | single | digit | displays | 9 | , | and | the | tens | digit | displays | 2 | . | Round | down | (floor) | : | take | only | the | integer | part | of | the | value | .

Practice | Programming | logo | 03 | Judgment | on | whether | to | press | the | button | Button | judgment | is | used | to | determine | when | to | start | the | countdown | . | You | can | set | the | countdown | value | before | pressing | the | key, | and | the | countdown | will | start | after | pressing | the | key | . | In | order | to | avoid | negative | numbers | in | the | countdown, | it | is | necessary | to | perform | absolute | value | calculations | and | then | round | down | . | Absolute | value | operation | : | It | does | not | distinguish | between | positive | and | negative | values, | and | they | are | unified | as | positive | numbers | . | Pay | attention | to | distinguishing | the | concepts | of | absolute | value | operation | and | absolute | value | .

Further Reading | The | clocks | and | watches | that | people | usually | use | have | an | error | of | about | 1 | minute | per | year | with | high | precision, | which | has | no | effect | on | daily | life, | but | more | accurate | timing | tools | are | needed | in | demanding | production | and | scientific | research | . | At | present, | the | most | accurate | timekeeping | tool | in | the | world | is | the | atomic | clock, | which | appeared | in | the | 1950 | s | . | Atomic | clocks | keep | time | by | using | electromagnetic | waves | emitted | when | atoms | absorb | or | release | energy | . | Because | this | electromagnetic | wave | is | very | stable | and | controlled | by | a | series | of | sophisticated | instruments, | the | timing | of | atomic | clocks | can | be | very | accurate | . | The | elements | currently | used | in | atomic | clocks | include | Hydrogen, | Cesium, | and | Rubidium | . | Atomic | clocks | are | accurate | to | only | 1 | second | every | 20 | million | years | . | This | provides | a | strong | guarantee | for | astronomy, | navigation, | and | space | navigation | .
